title: Can I SURVIVE Drawback Chess?
summary: Drawback Chess (third drawback video) on the drawback-chess website against anonymous online humans: each player has a random secret drawback; this time he does NOT reveal his. Goal: win five games. Drawbacks he got: Leveling Up (G1), Stand Your Ground (G2), Botez Gambit (G3, sacrificed the queen before move 11), Even Keeled (G4), Spread Out (G5). Opponents' drawbacks revealed on the post-game info board: True Love, Shell Shocked, Cowering in Fear, Savior Complex, Monkey See. He wins all five, mostly by capturing the king.
rules: Standard start. Each player is assigned one random secret drawback, revealed on an 'info board' after the game.
No check/checkmate: you win by CAPTURING the enemy king; you may castle out of or move into check (6:20).
You also win if the opponent violates a 'lose' drawback (e.g. Savior Complex).

Drawbacks seen: Leveling Up - can't capture a piece type until you've captured its predecessor (pawn, knight, bishop, rook, queen, king); True Love - king may only move to squares adjacent to its queen (and queen next to king); Stand Your Ground - your pieces can only capture if they are attacked; Shell Shocked - when the opponent captures, your pieces adjacent to the capture can't move for one turn; Botez Gambit - at the start of turn 11 you must have no queen and the opponent must have a queen; Cowering in Fear - (can't move a piece ... toward attackers; text cut off); Even Keeled - you can only capture on even-numbered moves; Savior Complex - when in check you must move your queen or you lose; Spread Out - you can't move a non-pawn piece adjacent to another of your non-pawn pieces; Monkey See - you can only capture with piece types your opponent has captured with.
Site shows a difficulty rating for each drawback (easy-hard slider).
win_condition: Capture the enemy king (or opponent loses via drawback / time). Series goal: 5 wins.
